name: Rob Walton
forbes_bio: Rob Walton is the eldest son of Walmart founder Sam Walton.
Walton took over as chairman upon his father's death in 1992.
He retired as chairman in 2015 and was replaced by his son-in-law, Greg Penner. Walton retired from Walmart's board in 2024.
He and other heirs of Sam Walton collectively own about 45% of Walmart's stock.
In 2022, a group led by Walton bought the NFL's Denver Broncos for $4.7 billion. Walton transferred controlling ownership of the team to his son-in-law Greg Penner in 2023.
forbes_facts: Rob Walton, who has a law degree from Columbia University, helped Walmart prepare for its IPO in 1970.
His daughter Carrie Walton Penner sits on the board of the Walton Family Foundation, which his parents set up on Walmart's 25th anniversary in 1987.

name: John Tu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Kingston Technology CEO John Tu runs the firm, which makes storage and memory products, from a cubicle on sales floor.
With longtime partner David Sun, Tu launched a computer memory business out of a garage and sold it to now defunct PC maker AST a few years later.
After losing a fortune in the stock market in 1987, the pair started Kingston to manufacture surface-mount memory chips.
Tu, a Chinese native who grew up in Taiwan, got an engineering degree in Germany and then immigrated to the U.S. in 1971.
Tu's first jobs in the U.S. included running a one-man gift shop with imported Chinese collectibles and selling commercial real estate.
forbes_facts: Tu met his business partner David Sun, who is 10 years his junior, at a basketball league.
The company's name comes from one of John Tu's favorite bands, the Kingston Trio.

name: Josh Kushner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026)
forbes_bio: Josh Kushner founded and runs VC firm Thrive Capital, which has backed some of the past decade's most notable startups, including Instagram, Spotify, Stripe and OpenAI.
Thrive was last valued at $5.3 billion in a $175 million funding round in January 2023; Kushner is estimated to own a 66% stake.
Thrive's investors include Disney CEO Bob Iger and a handful of billionaires: Henry Kravis, Mukesh Ambani, Jorge Paulo Lemann and Xavier Niel.
Thrive raised $10 billion for its tenth fund in February 2026; the firm now manages more than $65 billion in assets.
In August 2026, Kushner and Thrive Capital agreed a deal to purchase the NBA's L.A. Lakers for $12.5 billion alongside former Disney CEO Bob Iger.
He is the son of real estate tycoon Charles Kushner, who became Trump's ambassador to France in May 2025.
forbes_facts: Thrive's headquarters are in NYC's Puck Building, owned by the Kushner family, where Josh and his wife, model Karlie Kloss, also live in a penthouse.
The liberal Kushner cofounded a health insurance company built around Obamacare before his brother Jared's father-in-law Donald Trump became president.

name: Simon Reuben
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Simon Reuben shares a real estate, technology and investment fortune with his brother David Reuben.
In 2016, they sold 49% of their data center business, GlobalSwitch, to a consortium of Chinese investors for nearly $3 billion.
They sold a further 25% of the business in 2018 for $2.7 billion to a consortium of Asian institutional and private investors for $2.7 billion.
The brothers were born in Mumbai and raised in the U.K., where David started off trading metals and Simon imported carpets and bought real estate.
Their firm Transworld, a metals trader, invested in Russia and Kazakhstan in the 1990s and was active in trading aluminum.
The Reuben family owns an estimated 14% of Premier League's Newcastle United F.C.

name: Gayle Benson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Gayle Benson is the widow of Tom Benson (d. March 2018), former owner of the NFL New Orleans Saints and NBA New Orleans Pelicans.
She inherited both teams, after a multi-year dispute with Tom's daughter and grandchildren over control of family assets.
Family members sued, claiming Tom was mentally incompetent; the parties ended the dispute in early 2017 with a confidential settlement.
Gayle worked as an interior designer starting in the 1970s and founded thoroughbred horse racing company GMB Racing in 2014.
Gayle and Tom married in October 2004. She was his third wife.

name: Sulaiman Al Habib
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Sulaiman Al Habib is the founder and chairman of Riyadh-based hospital group Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Services Group, known as HMG.
Al Habib, a trained pediatrician, founded the group in 1995 and took it public on the Saudi stock exchange in 2020; he owns a 40% stake.
The group owns and runs hospitals and medical clinics in several cities in Saudi Arabia as well as in Dubai and Bahrain; it also operates a chain of pharmacies.
In addition to traditional hospitals, the group has centers specialized in fertility, dermatology, plastic surgery, obesity treatment and more.
In the late 1980s, Al Habib served as the head of the pediatrics department at the Security Forces Hospital in Riyadh.

name: Piero Ferrari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Piero Ferrari is vice chairman and 10% owner of luxury race car company Ferrari. His father Enzo founded Ferrari.
Piero became a billionaire when Ferrari listed its shares on the New York Stock Exchange in October 2015.
The company went public as part of a spinoff from Fiat Chrysler.
He became the sole heir after his stepbrother and Enzo's first son, Alfredo "Dino" Ferrari, died from muscular dystrophy in 1956.
Piero actively supports Centro Dino Ferrari, a research center for muscular and neurodegenerative diseases that his father cofounded in Dino's memory.
forbes_facts: Piero owns several yachts and owns a stake in Italian luxury yacht builder Ferretti Group.
He was reportedly not legally recognized as part of the Ferrari family until after the death of Enzo's wife, Laura, in 1978.

name: Joseph Liemandt
forbes_bio: Joe Liemandt is the founder of ESW Capital, an investment firm that purchases software companies.
ESW Capital has purchased more than 100 small U.S. software companies with a strategy of moving their workforce to foreign freelance workers.
Liemandt is known for founding Trilogy Software, a product and sales configuration software company that was prominent in the 1990s.
He dropped out of Stanford to start Trilogy Software. By age 27, he was on the cover of Forbes magazine.
A few months later, he appeared as the youngest self-made member of the 1996 issue of The Forbes 400, with a $500 million net worth.

name: Anna Viegener
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Anna Viegener chairs Viega, a German maker of plumbing and HVAC systems and products.
Founded in 1899, the Viega family fortune is now in its fifth generation and has manufacturing facilities in the U.S., India, China and Switzerland.
Viegener sits on the board of the Viega Foundation, which supports organizations that are working toward clean water and sanitation.
The company employs 5,000 people worldwide.
Her cousin, Franz Viegener, a fellow billionaire, is also involved in the business.

name: Thomas Straumann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Thomas Straumann owns a 17% stake in the world's largest manufacturer of dental implants, publicly held Straumann Holding.
Straumann's grandfather Reinhard founded the company in 1954 as an alloy research company that developed implants to treat bone fractures.
Straumann's father Fritz met real success during the 1970s with the introduction of titanium dental implants.
Straumann joined the company's board of directors in 1990 and shifted the firm's focus to dental products only.
Straumann chairs Medartis, a publicly traded medical device outfit that he founded in 1997.
forbes_facts: Straumann owns the luxurious Hotel Les Trois Roi in Basel, Switzerland.
Straumann, whose daughter Flaminia is a professional rider, owns a stable of jumping horses.

name: David MacNeil
forbes_bio: David MacNeil founded the automotive accessories company WeatherTech in 1989.
WeatherTech, which manufactures all of its products in the United States, generated $800 million in revenues in 2025.
Known for its car floor mats, WeatherTech has expanded into home goods in recent years.
In January 2026, President Trump nominated MacNeil to the Federal Trade Commission. His confirmation is pending.
MacNeil owns a vintage car collection worth over $400 million. It includes one of the most expensive cars in the world: a 1963 Ferrari 250 GTO, which he bought in 2018 for an estimated $75 million.
forbes_facts: MacNeil is a certified airline transport pilot who's flown to 39 countries.
MacNeil is also a bronze-rated FIA driver, and his son Cooper is a retired professional racer.
